definition.en-US: Git is a version control system that records the history of changes to a folder of files, so you can return to an earlier state.

analogy.en-US: It works like a notebook that keeps every draft of a recipe, so you can go back to the version that tasted best.

definition.en-US: A repository is a project together with the complete record of how each of its files has changed.

analogy.en-US: It is like a recipe binder that holds each recipe card together with every earlier draft of that card.

definition.en-US: A commit is a saved checkpoint that records the changes to one or more files, together with a message that says what changed.

analogy.en-US: It is like a save point in a video game, which you can load again if the next part goes wrong.

definition.en-US: GitHub Desktop is a free app from GitHub that lets you do Git work with buttons and menus instead of typed commands.

analogy.en-US: It is like a car dashboard, which shows what the engine is doing in clear dials so you never have to look under the hood.

definition.en-US: A remote repository is the copy of a repository that is stored on GitHub, where anyone with access can reach it over the internet.

analogy.en-US: It is like a shared document stored in an online drive, where everyone who has been given access can open the same version.

definition.en-US: To clone a repository means to make a complete copy of it on your computer, including its history.

analogy.en-US: It is like photocopying a whole book, margin notes included, so that you can write in your own copy.

definition.en-US: A local repository is the copy of a repository on your own computer, where you make changes before you send them to GitHub.

analogy.en-US: It is like a draft you keep on your own desk, which you can edit freely before you send the final version to the shared office.

definition.en-US: To push means to send your saved commits from your computer to the remote repository on GitHub.

analogy.en-US: It is like posting a finished letter to the family group chat, so that the others can read it too.

definition.en-US: A diff is a view that shows which lines of a file were added, removed or changed since the last saved version.

analogy.en-US: It is like a teacher's red-pen marks on an essay, showing exactly which sentences were added or crossed out.

definition.en-US: To revert a commit means to create a new commit that cancels its changes, while the original commit stays in the history.

analogy.en-US: It is like a refund for a purchase: the refund is a new record, and the original purchase is still in your books.

definition.en-US: To reset to a commit means to move the branch back to an older commit that has not been pushed, and bring the later changes back into your working files.

analogy.en-US: It is like taking a book back to an earlier chapter, with the later pages in your hands so you can reread them or tear them out.
